questions.text: Elements in the same vertical column of the periodic table are called ____.

options.option_text: periods — horizontal rows across the table
groups or families — share valence electron count
isotopes — same element, different mass numbers
isomers — same formula, different structures

questions.explanation: Vertical columns = groups (or families); horizontal rows = periods. Elements in the same group share the same number of valence electrons and exhibit similar chemical properties. There are 18 groups and 7 periods in the modern periodic table.

questions.text: Noble gases (Group 18) are chemically inert primarily because they have ____.

options.option_text: very high atomic masses that resist bonding
a completely filled outermost electron shell
no neutrons in their nucleus at all
extremely low melting points below absolute zero

questions.explanation: Noble gases have 8 electrons in their outermost shell (2 for helium), achieving stable 'octet' (or duet) configuration. This full valence shell means they have no tendency to gain or lose electrons — hence their chemical inertness. Helium (2), Neon (2,8), Argon (2,8,8) all follow this rule.

questions.text: Across a period from left to right in the modern periodic table, atomic radius generally ____.

options.option_text: increases steadily because electrons are added to successive shells
remains constant since all electrons enter the same energy shell
decreases due to increasing nuclear charge pulling electrons inward
first decreases then increases sharply at transition metals

questions.explanation: Moving left to right across a period, the nuclear charge (proton count) increases while electrons are added to the SAME shell. The stronger nuclear attraction contracts the electron cloud, steadily reducing atomic radius. Atomic radius increases DOWN a group because additional shells are added further from the nucleus.

questions.text: Mendeleev predicted an undiscovered element he called 'eka-silicon' (atomic mass ~72). It was later discovered and named ____.

options.option_text: Silicon (Si) — element directly below carbon in Group 14
Germanium (Ge) — confirmed all of Mendeleev's predictions
Gallium (Ga) — Mendeleev's predicted eka-boron
Scandium (Sc) — Mendeleev's predicted eka-aluminium

questions.explanation: Mendeleev's 'eka-silicon' (below silicon in Group 14) was discovered in 1886 and named Germanium — its properties matched Mendeleev's predictions almost exactly. He also predicted eka-aluminium (→ Gallium, 1875) and eka-boron (→ Scandium, 1879). These discoveries validated the periodic law.

questions.text: Alkali metals (Group 1) are highly reactive because ____.

options.option_text: they have a full outer shell and strongly resist bonding
they have one valence electron that is very easily lost
they have the highest electronegativities in their periods
they form stable covalent bonds readily with water molecules

questions.explanation: Group 1 metals have 1 valence electron and very low ionisation energies — they readily donate this electron to form +1 ions (e.g., Na → Na⁺). Reactivity increases down the group (Li < Na < K < Rb < Cs) as the valence electron sits farther from the nucleus and is lost even more easily.

questions.text: Across Period 3 (Na to Cl), which of the following trends is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Ionisation energy generally increases from Na to Cl
Electronegativity decreases from Na to Cl across the period
Metallic character decreases from Na to Cl progressively
Non-metallic character increases from Na to Cl progressively

questions.explanation: Electronegativity INCREASES left to right across a period (Na 0.93 → Cl 3.16) because the nuclear charge rises while the shell stays the same, pulling bonding electrons more strongly. All other options state correct Period 3 trends: ionisation energy generally rises (with minor dips at Mg→Al and P→S), metallic character falls, non-metallic character rises.

questions.text: Element X has atomic number 17. Its electronic configuration (2, 8, 7) places it in ____.

options.option_text: Group 1, Period 3 — a reactive alkali metal
Group 17, Period 3 — a halogen (Chlorine)
Group 16, Period 3 — a chalcogen, like sulphur
Group 18, Period 3 — a noble gas with full shell

questions.explanation: Atomic number 17 = Chlorine. Configuration 2, 8, 7: three shells → Period 3; 7 valence electrons → Group 17 (halogens). Halogens are one electron short of a noble gas configuration, making them strongly electronegative. They exist as diatomic molecules (Cl₂) and form −1 ions (Cl⁻) readily.
